pr_title: swc_ecma_parser: fix #9227: allow escaped keywords as an object property name
pr_body:
<!-- Note: CI script will automatically rebase your PR so please do not rebase unless required -->

<!-- Thanks for submitting a pull request! Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. -->

**Description:**

With this PR, the lexer error `SyntaxError::EscapeInReservedWord` is un-done at the parser level if the reserved words appears as an object property name.

The bug in #9227 only happens because the first "peek" in the lexer happens when context has `in_property_name` that's still _false_, so there is no chance to disambiguate. (And I couldn't be sure that a change to this call didn't affect other cases; JavaScript's grammar is quite varied.)

[NOTE: I just noticed that there are a bunch more cases where \u escape codes should be allowed but aren't. This PR wont' be sufficient, adn the final fix will probably need a completely different approach.]
  
**This is a draft!**

I'm posting it to get some feedback on whether this is going in the right direction.

There are also a few open points:

- [ ] _Negative tests_. I'd like to add a negative test (expected to fail) under _tests/js_. Is this even possible?
- [ ] _TODO: obj.v\u0061r_. Feature: apply the same fix to property names in positions other than object literals (e.g. `obj.\u0063ontinue`)
- [ ] _"Unget token"_. Should we refactor the "replace token" logic that's currently implemented with p.input.cur() then p.input.store()? Something like `p.input.unget(token)`
- [ ] _More general design_. The bug is roughly in the pattern: "lex with ctx A; then start parsing with slightly different ctx B", but an error in ctx A is not an error in B. Is it worth it to make a more general change? I can think of:
  1. make the lexer fully independent of context (probably not practical)
  1. add a mechanism where the lexer can detect that an error was due to ctx A and the context has changed since, so the lexing is repeated with ctx B. Not sure how hard this is.
 
**Related issue (if exists):** #9227

issue_context.title: swc_ecma_parser: Unexpected escape sequence in reserved word (2)
comments:
# GFI guide


```
37 | var obj = ({ v\u0061r: 42 });
```

This is about an object lieral, and the relevant code lives at


https://github.com/swc-project/swc/blob/1ec68cb5b198e0acac321266f6b606e6407d41eb/crates/swc_ecma_parser/src/parser/object.rs#L183-L212

It seems like `parse_prop_name` has a bug.

`parse_prop_name` is declared as

https://github.com/swc-project/swc/blob/1ec68cb5b198e0acac321266f6b606e6407d41eb/crates/swc_ecma_parser/src/parser/object.rs#L43-L122

But there's no relevant error reporting logic so my guess is that the error is from lexer. The relevant error reporting logic is at https://github.com/swc-project/swc/blob/1ec68cb5b198e0acac321266f6b606e6407d41eb/crates/swc_ecma_parser/src/lexer/mod.rs#L777-L780

We need to patch this logic to allow escapes in reserved word in property names.
I'm going to take a stab at it

Fixing this bug is not as simple as adding a new context flag. Since swc parser reads next token automatically when last token is taken, we can't figure out where to add the new context flag. 

Specifically, I think the token reading happens at:
https://github.com/swc-project/swc/blob/c43dbad028072396390029af44e31bc3292a342a/crates/swc_ecma_parser/src/parser/object.rs#L27
We can't assume the parser is going to parse https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-LiteralPropertyName, therefore it is not proper to add the context flag there.

Yes, that's what I figured. I also tried "forwarding" richer info downstream of the lexer (PR #9236), so that the identifier/keyword ambiguity can be resolved in a later phase, but it seems to be a dead end.

(In an unrelated note: I've kind of given up on this bug. I've been focusing on other stuff since, and this bug isn't really bothering me much. I'm not sure how much more I can contribute here; looks like the necessary effort is out of reach for me now.)

review_comments: This is done so that, in addition to printing the word in an error message, the whole `Token` that caused the error can be 'put back into the parser'.
This entire logic could be refactored into a method in `Buffer`, something like `p.input.unget` (reusing the from the C; or maybe "unread" like in Go)
This change makes this PR a breaking change, so I think it's better to revert this.
This is the wrong direction. We should adjust `ctx` to ignore the error at the first place.
If by "adjusting ctx" you mean adding `with_ctx({ in_property_name: true, ... })` at the call site of a parser, I had initially thought it could have been too coarse... I need to try again.
I think adding a field for ignoring escapes in keywords to the context type is the best solution
